title: Making Uganda’s Hidden Stories Visible: My Wiki for Minorities 2026 Journey
content:
My name is Atim Sally Ruth, and I contribute to Wikimedia projects as ASally Ruth. I am a member of the Wikimedia Community User Group Uganda and, in 2026, I had the opportunity to support Wiki for Minorities in Uganda as part of the Core Organising Team (COT), with a primary focus on communications. My fellow COT members were Sandra Aceng, Emmy Okwir and Emmanuel Oruk.

Running from 30 April to 17 July 2026, Wiki for Minorities brought together contributors and supporters around an important shared goal: strengthening the visibility and documentation of Uganda’s underrepresented communities, cultures, languages, and environmental heritage.

Uganda is home to remarkable cultural, linguistic, and environmental diversity. Yet much of this knowledge remains underrepresented online. For me, Wiki for Minorities is an important response to that gap.

title: 72 Hours Virtual Marathon Edit-a-thon in the Igbo Wikimedians User Group – July 2026 Edition
content:
The Igbo Wikimedians User Group’s 72 hours virtual marathon edit-a-thon once again advanced the mission of preserving the Igbo language through open knowledge, emphasizing quality contributions over sheer volume. Launched in April 2025, the project has achieved notable success thanks to community-wide collaboration and active participation. This edition in July 2026 built on the already established efforts and further strengthened editor’s skill.

We kicked off with our standard orientation session, helping participants get comfortable with the workflow and understand their assigned tasks. As organizers, we practically demonstrated translations on Translatewiki.net while re-emphasizing quality over quantity. We also showed how to correct reference errors, add the Databox and DEFAULTSORT templates to pages. From 28 to 31 July 2026, editors committed 72 hours to enhancing the Igbo Wikipedia. Throughout the marathon, participants concentrated specifically on:

  • Adding {{DEFAULTSORT}} and {{Databox}} to biography pages for better organization and accessibility.
  • Fixing reference errors in Igbo Wikipedia to ensure integrity.
  • Completing translations on Translatewiki.net

title: The Pre-Conference on Information Integrity in Climate Change at Wikimania
content: During Wikimania in Paris, the Working Group on Climate Justice and Wikimedia Projects, together with Wikimedia Brazil and in collaboration with the Wikimedia Foundation, organized the Pre-Conference on Information Integrity in Climate Change, with the goal of building strategic coalitions around information integrity, a concept that refers to ensuring that data is accurate, complete, consistent, and understandable.

title: Wikimedia at Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science 2026 Uyo, Nigeria
content:
Twenty researchers, educators, health professionals, students, and practitioners gathered in Uyo with different research interests but a shared task: to learn how computational methods could help them investigate social problems more carefully.

For fourteen days, the Summer Institute in Computational Social Science Nigeria 2026 brought participants together under the theme “Tech for Open Minds.” The programme combined discussions on misinformation, gender bias, public health, education, digital inclusion, and knowledge inequality with practical training in data collection and analysis.

For many participants, it was also an opportunity to discover Wikimedia beyond reading Wikipedia articles.

The Summer Institute in Computational Social Science was founded by Professors Christopher Bail and Matthew Salganik, the SICSS Nigeria 2026 – Uyo experience was sponsored by the Templeton World Charity Foundation and Wiki In Africa. Hosted by Dr Rhoda Asuquo, with Dr Juliet Inyang and Yohanna Joseph Waliya as co-hosts. A handpicked group of exceptional facilitators facilitated each session, all experts in their respective fields.

title: Opening Access to Cultural Heritage through Digitalization and Wikimedia Commons
content:
In 2025, Wikimedia Indonesia, through the GLAM Indonesia Grant, supported several projects that bring together cultural preservation work with digital technology. This program is aimed at researchers, practitioners of art and culture, archivists, and communities working in the fields of galleries, libraries, archives, and museums. One of the program’s goals is to produce works that can be openly shared with the public through Wikimedia projects.

In its implementation, the two GLAM Indonesia 2025 Grant projects demonstrate different approaches to reopening access to cultural heritage. Illuminating Manuscript Ornament: From Royal Frames to Digital Commons processes the ornamental designs of Nusantara manuscripts into open digital visual assets. Meanwhile, the Digital Archiving for Banda Cultural Museum focuses on the documentation and digital archiving of a museum’s collection in Banda Neira.

title: How Learning About Capital Letters Brought Wikipedia Into My Classroom
content:
On August 19, 2026, I taught my Bahasa Indonesia class a lesson on capital letters, huruf kapital. On paper, it was an ordinary grammar lesson. For me, it was something I had been waiting for since long before I ever stood in front of a classroom.

I am a Wikimedian and an elementary school teacher from Indonesia. I have spent years believing in this movement, in free knowledge, in the idea that anyone can edit and anyone can learn. But for just as long, I have carried a quiet worry, that Wikipedia’s impact, for all its scale, often stays trapped inside the internet. It’s everywhere, and yet at the grassroots level, in a classroom, in a small village, in the hands of a child, it can still feel invisible. This year, as a brand-new teacher, I finally had a chance to close that gap myself.

title: Wiki ASEAN Day Talk 2026: Encouraging ASEAN Youth to Take on a Role in the Digital Knowledge Ecosystem
content:
Saturday, August 8th 2026. Coinciding with ASEAN Day, KlubWiki Universitas Brawijaya held the online event Wiki ASEAN Day Talk 2026 via Zoom. This talkshow was a part of Wiki ASEAN Day 2026, a regional initiative by KlubWiki UB in support of the main theme to the 2026 ASEAN Summit, “Navigating Our Future, Together”. Wiki ASEAN Day 2026 focuses on youth empowerment, in line with the People Empowerment pillar of the ASEAN Community Vision 2045, ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community sphere.The event was opened by MC Kesya Stevany Santoso and led by discussion moderator Jeremiah Martin, both members of KlubWiki Universitas Brawijaya.

Kanyadibya Cendana Prasetyo, advisor to KlubWiki Universitas Brawijaya and lecturer of the International Relations programme at Brawijaya University, expressed how Wiki ASEAN Day is an important presence in raising awareness and creating a sense of belonging towards ASEAN among Wikimedia contributors across Southeast Asia. She stated, “I think Wiki ASEAN Day is a significant event in promoting ASEAN and nurturing a sense of belonging as fellow ASEAN citizens among Wikimedia contributors in Southeast Asia.”

title: Wikiversity at 20: Learning in the Open
content:
On 15 August 2006, Wikiversity opened a new space within the Wikimedia movement: a place where people could not only access educational resources, but also create, share, and participate in learning together.

Wikiversity had grown out of work within Wikibooks and became an independent Wikimedia project in August 2006. Its creation expanded the educational possibilities of the movement beyond textbooks, with a focus on both learning resources and learning activities in English and other languages.

Twenty years later, that idea remains at the heart of Wikiversity.

Its motto, “Set learning free,” captures an approach to education built around participation, collaboration, open resources, and the ability for learners and educators to shape the learning environment themselves.

One of the simplest ways to use Wikiversity is to find and adapt learning resources. The project hosts lesson plans, course notes, reading lists, problem sets, activities, simulations, teaching aids, and other materials that educators and learners can use and develop.

title: How AWA is Growing Skills, Community, and Confidence Across the African Wikimedian Space
content:
Across Africa, teaching people how to edit Wikipedia is only the beginning. Africa Wikipedian Alliance (AWA)’s learning programme is exploring what contributors need to stay, grow and eventually lead.

Opening a Wikipedia account is easy. Learning to use it well is not.

A new contributor must learn how to judge the reliability of a source, navigate unfamiliar editing tools and make changes without disrupting the work of others. This often brings up harder questions. How should an editor respond to artificial intelligence that produces polished prose and invented citations with equal confidence? How can a patroller protect Wikipedia from vandalism without driving away a beginner who has made an honest mistake? What does it take for an African language to become not merely visible online, but usable across the systems on which digital knowledge increasingly depends?

These questions are at the heart of the work of the African Wikipedian Alliance (AWA): building communities capable of creating, protecting and sustaining their own knowledge.
snippet: Across Africa, teaching people how to edit Wikipedia is only the beginning. Africa Wikipedian Alliance (AWA)’s learning programme is exploring what contributors need to stay, grow and eventually lead.
creator: Bukola James

title: Igala Wikimedia Campus Outreach
content:
The Igala Wikimedia Campus Outreach was successfully implemented across three higher institutions in Kogi State:

  • Kogi state Polytechnic Lokoja
  • Federal Polytechnic Idah
  • Prince Abubakar Audu University, Anyigba

    • The outreach served as a capacity-building initiative designed to recruit, train, and mentor new Wikimedia contributors while promoting the documentation of Igala language, culture, history, and notable personalities on Wikimedia platforms. Through practical editing sessions, mentorship, and collaborative learning, participants gained the skills required to contribute quality knowledge to Wikipedia and related Wikimedia projects.

    The primary objective of the outreach was to increase the number of active Igala Wikimedia editors and improve the availability of Igala-related knowledge on Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. Specifically, the project sought to:

  • Train new editors in Wikipedia editing and Wikimedia policies.
  • Increase the number of contributors to the Igala Wikimedia community.
  • Document and preserve Igala language, culture, history, and notable personalities.
  • Improve the quality and accessibility of Igala-related content online.
